newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - 8 tests in 11 weeks for 1997 All Blacks.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - 8 tests in 11 weeks for 1997 All Blacks.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Nov 11 - The All Blacks will play eight tests in 11 weeks during their 1997 international campaign, NZPA reported on Monday.

The organising body of the southern hemisphere tri-series, Sanzar, is due to release details of both the test matches between Australia, New Zealand and South Africa, and the Super 12 programme next Friday.
However the tri-series dates were leaked today and show a similar format to this year.
In 1996, the All Blacks played 10 tests in 13 weeks.
All Black coach John Hart had wanted a two-week break between the end of the home tests against Fiji and Argentina and travelling to South Africa for the start of the tri-series on July 19.
While he got that, the two-week gap he wanted between the home test against South Africa on August 9 and the test against Australia in Dunedin has been cut to one.
Member unions have been worried about the effect on their national championship gates and also about the loss of their All Blacks for a further week. The Dunedin test will be on August 16.
"It'll be tough again, there's no doubt about that," Hart said today.
"It's desirable to have a two-week break between tests where possible, but inevitably with a competition as compressed as it is at present sides will have to play some games weekly."
Hart is looking forward to the July 26 test in Australian Rules-mad Melbourne, suggesting the All Blacks will feel more at home there than at the Sydney Football Stadium.
"It's not a bad thing -- a bit of a neutral ground, really," he said.
The Australian Rugby Union are hoping for a crowd of close to 90,000.
About 80,000 watched New Zealand beat Australia in the 1991 rugby league test at the ground.
New Zealand Rugby Football Union chief executive David Moffett was angry that the dates had been released early.
"I'm flabbergasted that anybody has released information about this when there was an agreement it should not be released until next Friday," he said.
Tri-series dates:
July 19: All Blacks v South Africa, Pretoria.
July 26: New Zealand v Australia, Melbourne.
August 2: Australia v South Africa, Brisbane.
August 9: All Blacks v South Africa, Auckland.
August 16: New Zealand v Australia, Dunedin.
August 23: South Africa v Australia, Johannesburg.
The unconfirmed dates for the All Blacks other tests are believed to be:
June 14: v Fiji, Hamilton.
June 21: v Argentina, Wellington.
June 28: v Argentina, Albany.
July 5: v Australia (Bledisloe Cup), Christchurch.
The All Blacks also have end-of-year tests against Wales and England.
